text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United Nations Secretary-general is due to issue invitations for direct talks between the two sides by the end of May.

- Socialist Edek is due to meet communist Akel today with a proposal to field Greek deputy foreign minister Yannos Kranidiotis (a Cypriot) as the opposition's candidate in the presidential elections scheduled early next year.
- Parliament is heading towards a new postponement of a vote for scrapping a ban on homosexuality.

- The Attorney-general orders the release of an Armenian woman who was arrested as an illegal immigrant when she went to a police station to collect her missing son. The woman is under United Nations protection.
- Where, when and how? Under Secretary-general Sir Kieran Prendergast is due to discuss these issues still pending regarding the high level meeting between the two sides scheduled for June.
- The resumption of direct talks on the Cyprus dispute are to take place in New York and continue in Geneva.
- Sewerage is spilling into the streets in some areas of Nicosia due to the absence of a sewerage system.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash telephoned the presidential palace on Tuesday morning after President Glafcos Clerides was admitted to hospital and wished him a speedy recovery.
- The Clerides-Denktash meeting is set for June.
- The foreign ministry is due to start promoting the issue of Cyprus's missing persons at an international level.
